messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: log_prob methods in compiled model
parts:
After parsing through stanc, the cpp for my models includes the signature

var log_prob(vector<var>& params_r__, vector<int>& params_i__, std::ostream* pstream__ = 0)

but not the signature

double log_prob(vector<double>& params_r__, vector<int>& params_i__, std::ostream* pstream__ = 0)

which makes testing/debugging difficult. And also difficult to understand how the current MCMC implementations work, as they all call the double version. Is this the intended behavior, or did I misspecify something in the parsing?

Thanks.

-Betancourt

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] log_prob methods in compiled model
parts:
In the current release (1.2.0) version, the superclass
prob_grad_ad of the model class implements the log_prob
method for double by calling the virtual log_prob method
declared for agrad::var types.

In the refactored code on the main branch, there's a templated
function that can be used for double or var.

BUT: The double version won't use the propto calcs, so
the log prob values returned will be different (by a constant
that doesn't depend on the parameter values).

But now that I think about it, I don't know which one will
be called. There's a non-template virtual in prob_grad_ad:

virtual double log_prob(std::vector<double>& params_r,
std::vector<int>& params_i,
std::ostream* output_stream = 0) { ...

and then a template in the generated code for the model class:

template <typename T>
T log_prob(std::vector<T>& params_r,
std::vector<int>& params_i,
std::ostream* output_stream = 0)


The current sampling implementations don't need the double
version.

- Bob

> The current sampling implementations don't need the double

I'm confused -- isn't the double version being called in the leapfrog implementations?

double nondiag_leapfrog(stan::model::prob_grad& model,
std::vector<int> z,
const Eigen::MatrixXd& _cov_L,
std::vector<double>& x, std::vector<double>& m,
std::vector<double>& g, double epsilon,
std::ostream* error_msgs = 0,
std::ostream* output_msgs = 0) {
Eigen::Map<Eigen::VectorXd> x_mat(&x[0],x.size());
Eigen::Map<Eigen::VectorXd> m_mat(&m[0],m.size());
Eigen::Map<Eigen::VectorXd> g_mat(&g[0],g.size());
m_mat += (0.5 * epsilon) * (_cov_L.transpose().triangularView<Eigen::Upper>() * g_mat);
x_mat += epsilon * (_cov_L.triangularView<Eigen::Lower>() * m_mat);
double logp;
try {
logp = model.grad_log_prob(x, z, g, output_msgs);
} catch (std::domain_error e) {
write_error_msgs(error_msgs,e);
logp = -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
}
m_mat += (0.5 * epsilon) * (_cov_L.transpose().triangularView<Eigen::Upper>() * g_mat);
return logp;
}

calls the var version in order to compute the gradients and the

To figure this out, you need to look where the function is
defined (grad_log_prob, that is), then check what it calls.
You'll see the var version getting called.

With the new code generator, you're going to need to
provide a propto argument, too. You can be very
explicit about the double arg, too:

model.log_prob<true,double>(x,w);

Also, I want to point out again that calling this
with doubles will give you different results because
the var version drops things up to a proportion.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] log_prob methods in compiled model
parts:
The issue is that our generated model hides the base class's methods:

http://www.parashift.com/c++-faq-lite/hiding-rule.html

log_prob() is being hidden away. Should we add lines like "using prob_grad_ad::log_prob;" in our generated code? This will unhide log_prob(). In the current generated code, we don't have this problem since log_prob() is defined multiple times, but I could see how this could bite us again in the future.

Thoughts?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] log_prob methods in compiled model
parts:
Damn that C++ type inference. Makes sense
Once I realized we were defining the function as
an abstract (pure) virtual function and also
as a template function.

On 3/25/13 2:59 PM, Daniel Lee wrote:
> The issue is that our generated model hides the base class's methods:
>
> http://www.parashift.com/c++-faq-lite/hiding-rule.html

My bad --- I should've foreseen the can of worms that
would be opened up by having the template function competing
with the abstract virtual function in the base class.
> log_prob() is being hidden away. Should we add lines like "using prob_grad_ad::log_prob;" in our generated code?

Will that still let us use the method template with
specified arguments?

We could also rename the templated function that's
generated and then have the template function called
by log_prob.

> This
> will unhide log_prob(). In the current generated code, we don't have this problem since log_prob() is defined multiple
> times, but I could see how this could bite us again in the future.

I think this is all too dangerous. I'd rather rename
to avoid confusion for us and clients.

> Thoughts?

The big issue in my mind is the propto calculations
which currently behave as follows in the templated
code (the first template parameter is propto and
the second is scalar type of parameters):

log_prob<true,double> : always return 0
log_prob<true,var> : drop constant terms
log_prob<false,double> : don't drop any terms
log_prob<false,var> : don't drop any terms

We use propto=true to speed up computations.

I think this is really confusing but I don't see any way around
this the way we're currently calculating propto based on
type.

- Bob
